precepts.point: The commentary says it plainly: false teachers who sound impressive, grand, polished, even spiritual, but hollow; style over truth, eloquence without substance.

note.label: Untruthful Trinity Revisited & Ridiculous

precepts.why:
Paul warned of them: “by good words and fair speeches deceive the hearts of the simple.” Good words and fair speeches: intellectual, big words, semantics, rhetoric. They serve theology; their theology is their god, and their own belly, money. Peter says the same: “For when they speak great swelling words of vanity, they allure through the lusts of the flesh”. There are no laws involved, no commandments involved.

The commentary on Peter says it: false teachers who sound impressive yet deliver nothing of substance. Homoousios, hypostatic, exegesis, ontological, hermeneutical, Christological: great swelling words. Their speech is grand, polished, well paced, even spiritual sounding, like Bible, but it is hollow, with no commandments, no responsibility, no accountability. Unlike Paul, who said “my speech and my preaching was not with enticing words of man’s wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power”. Paul refused persuasive words of man's wisdom; these teachers rely on style over truth, eloquence without gospel substance. In the Greek, great swelling words means great bulk: high sounding, but only words, vain and meaningless, with nothing but emptiness behind them.

Show me the scripture that says Christ is fully God and fully man. It isn't there. The word of God is plain and clear. Even their hermeneutics goes back to Schleiermacher, a German called the father of modern liberal theology, and Isaiah says “The vile person shall be no more called liberal”; the vile person will “utter error against the Lord, to make empty the soul of the hungry”. The word comes from Hermes, the Greek trickster god, so it is a trickster's interpretation, and the Jesuits carried it around the earth.

Peel back the swelling words and here is the premise: if Christ is fully God and fully man, only a two-essence being can keep God's laws, so we don't have to. But Christ said be perfect, as your Father in heaven is perfect, and Zacharias and Elisabeth walked “in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless.” It can be done. “The discourse of fools is irksome, and their sport is the wantonness of sin”: their sport is not having to keep the commandments.

precepts.text: And spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly. He was a preacher of God's laws. That is what righteous means. His laws. So Noah was preaching to the people, and the people mocked him and laughed at him.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

precepts.why:
Christ said “as the days of Noe were, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.” Noe is the Greek; it is still Noah. In his days they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, “until the day that Noe entered into the ark.” So what was Noah doing all that time? Peter tells us.

God “spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly.” Noah was a preacher of righteousness: a preacher of God's laws, because that is what righteous means, his laws. He was warning the people to repent and change their ways, and the people mocked him and laughed at him.

Then they “knew not until the flood came, and took them all away.” Took them away into what? Not the kingdom of heaven: destruction, death. Took is the past tense of take. So when Christ says “the one shall be taken, and the other left”, the one taken is taken to destruction, like the ungodly in the flood, and the one left is the righteous, like Noah.

So it shall be at Christ's coming: nations eating and drinking and carrying on, while those preaching God's laws are mocked, until the destruction comes on the world of the ungodly. “Therefore be ye also ready.”

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
“For if God spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment”. The angels that sinned are the sons of God in Genesis 6: Seth's line, that messed around with the daughters of men.

“And spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly”. What was Noah? A preacher of righteousness. So when 1 Peter says “the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing”, what was God doing? He was giving them time, and Noah was preaching repentance the whole while: y'all better repent, the Most High going to destroy this place. They said, you crazy. Look at that dummy building a boat for no reason.

Noah was prophesying all that time because God was longsuffering. He gave them a hundred years to repent, and they did not listen, and only “eight souls were saved by water”.

That is why Peter joins it to Christ, who was “put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit”: a man, not a demigod, brought back to life by the spirit after three days, who “went and preached unto the spirits in prison”. Those spirits in prison are his people, us in captivity. As Noah preached righteousness to a world that would not hear, Christ preached to his people in prison, and the longsuffering of God is waiting on us to repent the same way it waited in the days of Noah.

note.label: Woe to Amerikkka

precepts.why:
God “delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked”. Examine yourself: are you vexed with the filthy conversation of this world? Or are you up late scrolling, looking at booties, two hours in the middle of the night on your phone? Those two hours you could have read the Bible. If you can't sleep, pick up the Bible; half of one chapter and the demon will put you to sleep. In time the Most High will wake up your spirit, and you will read one, two, three, four chapters.

“For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day”. Every day you wake up you should be vexed with the filthy conversation of this world. But to be vexed, you have to be in this Bible. It is by having the word of God in you that sin starts becoming repulsive. If you are not reading and not studying, the sins of the world will be normal to you, just like everybody else. The Lord saved a remnant, and that is why we did not become as Sodom and Gomorrha. What is that remnant doing? Studying day and night.

Paul and Silas were sent by night unto Berea and went into the synagogue, and “These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.” If you are searching the scriptures daily, you will be vexed with the filthy conversation of this world. If you are not, whose words are going to be in your ears? The TV, the street, your phone: the ways of this world.

God turned Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes, “making them an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly”. America read the example and legalized gay marriage anyway, a habitual line stepper pushing the envelope until his sin reached the heavens. Only the one searching the scriptures daily will be vexed like Lot and delivered like Lot.

Stop listening to Esau, the pastors, preachers and congressmen talking about demons, Nephilim and fallen angels. That is a lie. This is the offspring of the sons of God. He “delivered them into chains of darkness”, and that is sin, “to be reserved unto judgment”, the same great day Jude talked about. “And spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly; And turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned them with an overthrow, making them an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly”. note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

precepts.why:
Manasseh begs, “forgive me, O Lord, forgive me, and destroy me not with mine iniquites. Be not angry with me for ever, by reserving evil for me.” What does he mean by reserving evil for you? There is evil reserved for you while you keep playing around. Peter shows it.

“For if God spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment.” These are the angels that fell in Adam’s time, cast down to destruction. Remember David said, take not thy holy spirit from me. If the Lord removes his Holy Spirit from you, you are now in chains of darkness, reserved unto judgment.

“The Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations, and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished.” Manasseh said, don’t reserve evil for me, because the Lord reserves punishment for the unjust. “But chiefly them that walk after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness, and despise government. Presumptuous are they, selfwilled, they are not afraid to speak evil of dignities.” Chiefly means primarily. Despising government is despising leadership. When leadership is trying to help you and you say, nah, I know what I’m doing, you are not humble. Your heart is arrogant.

They follow “the way of Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness”: money. “These are wells without water, clouds that are carried with a tempest”, carried about by different doctrines, all over the place, “to whom the mist of darkness is reserved for ever.” The mist of darkness is the reprobate mind; the Holy Spirit is not in them. That is evil reserved for them.

So Manasseh, a king worthy of that very judgment, humbled himself and asked the Lord not to reserve that evil for him. We must do the same while repentance is open.

note.label: Wars Are Here: Seek Good Not Evil

precepts.why:
God told Noah, “Come thou and all thy house into the ark; for thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation.” Why was Noah chosen to be delivered with his family? Peter explains it: God “spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly”.

The old world is the world we read about in Genesis 7, and God did not spare it: he killed all flesh. Noah was righteous because he preached righteousness and kept the commandments. He was a godly man in an ungodly world, and he had received his orders from God on exactly how to build the ark and did it faithfully. His standing up for God is what brought the flood in upon the ungodly.

Why is he called the eighth person? The other seven were his wife, his three sons, Shem, Ham and Japheth, and their wives. Noah is counted eighth because a true captain, a true leader, made sure his wife, his sons and their wives were on first, and he was the last one to get on the ark. When Noah gave the word, they did not question him; they got on.

That is why men of God have to be strong. We come to the Sabbath because we are sick. We are surrounded by the world all week and fighting the sin around us and in our own thoughts, so we need to be around brothers and sisters who will correct us in righteousness.

The flood shows the mind of God for destruction. Nobody was righteous except the ones on the ark. The coming destruction, a thermonuclear war, will be on another level, and we want to be spiritually the men and women in that ark, not the ones drowning. precepts.text: Three shepherds also I cut off in one month; my soul lothed them and their soul abhorred me: the Pharisees, Sadducees and scribes.
precepts.point: Leaders of other camps do not show up at IUIC schools unannounced and then complain on video about not being let in. There are channels; call first. The camps do not fellowship because of doctrine, and one GMS member sat in a school for months living a double life.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Peter describes men that “despise government” and “are not afraid to speak evil of dignities”, men with “eyes full of adultery”, “beguiling unstable souls”, with hearts “exercised with covetous practices”. “These are wells without water”, no understanding, “clouds that are carried with a tempest”, friends with this one, over there with that one, “to whom the mist of darkness is reserved for ever.” That same darkness is reserved for you when you hate your brother, and that is why they are confounded about Cornelius and Romans 11.

Zechariah shows the same kind of rulers in Christ's day: “Three shepherds also I cut off in one month”. The three shepherds are the Pharisees, the Sadducees and the scribes, the rulers, the builders. The Romans killed them. He says “my soul lothed them”: I hated them. And “their soul also abhorred me”: they hated me then.

So the evil speakers of 2 Peter 2 are the same spirit as the three shepherds: rulers who hated Christ and hated their own brothers, and God loathed them and cut them off. The dudes out here right now are doing the same thing they were doing back then, and that is how you will discover them.

precepts.text: Make the heart of this people fat and shut their eyes, lest they see and convert and be healed.
precepts.point: Leaders of other camps do not show up at IUIC schools unannounced and then complain on video about not being let in. There are channels; call first. The camps do not fellowship because of doctrine, and one GMS member sat in a school for months living a double life.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
The mist of darkness is reserved for those who speak evil of dignities and hate their brothers. Isaiah shows where that darkness comes from: “Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not. Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes”. Shut their eyes: darkness.

Why? “lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and convert, and be healed.” Convert means repent. Lest they repent. The Lord shuts the eyes of the builders, the rulers, so they cannot see.

That is why Peter calls them “wells without water”, with no understanding. When you badmouth Peter, Paul, John the Baptist or any of the apostles and prophets, the Lord puts the spirit of darkness on you until you become a borderline, if not full-blown, Christianity teacher. Your ears are made heavy and your eyes are shut, and you cannot understand even the basic verses. Be mindful how you deal with brothers; brothers who murmur and speak evil bug out and go back into the world.

precepts.text: Let them alone: they be blind leaders of the blind, and both shall fall into the ditch.
precepts.point: Leaders of other camps do not show up at IUIC schools unannounced and then complain on video about not being let in. There are channels; call first. The camps do not fellowship because of doctrine, and one GMS member sat in a school for months living a double life.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Christ said of the Pharisees: “Let them alone: they be blind leaders of the blind.” Leave them alone. “And if the blind lead the blind, both shall fall into the ditch”: snared and trapped.

In Matthew 23 Christ cursed them out the whole chapter: “Woe unto you, ye blind guides”. Keep that in mind: blinded, blind, eyes darkened, eyes shut. They say whosoever swears by the temple it is nothing, but whosoever swears by the gold of the temple is a debtor: they worry about money, hearts “exercised with covetous practices” as Peter says. “Ye fools and blind: for whether is greater, the gold, or the temple that sanctifieth the gold?”

The same blind leaders are around today, dark clothes, a dark spirit. That is why we do not come together with other camps: different doctrines, and some of those doctrines can lead you to damnation. Leaders of other camps who show up at our schools unannounced and then throw a tantrum on video for views show their real color. We don't show up at your house unannounced; there are channels, and you call first. A GMS member sat in one of our schools for months living a double life. We pray brothers get it right, but we let the blind leaders alone and keep doing the work.

precepts.text: Ye are of your father the devil. They answered, Say we not well that thou art a Samaritan and hast a devil? Samaritan was their insult, because they hated the northern kingdom.
precepts.point: Leaders of other camps do not show up at IUIC schools unannounced and then complain on video about not being let in. There are channels; call first. The camps do not fellowship because of doctrine, and one GMS member sat in a school for months living a double life.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
“Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him.” Christ is speaking to the elders, the rulers. “When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it.”

“And because I tell you the truth, ye believe me not.” “He that is of God heareth God’s words: ye therefore hear them not, because ye are not of God.” You elders of Satan.

Then watch the next verse: “Then answered the Jews, and said unto him, Say we not well that thou art a Samaritan, and hast a devil?” They called Christ a Samaritan because they hated the northern kingdom. Samaritan was a derogatory term to them: you're a Samaritan and a devil. Meanwhile they were planning to kill him. That's how evil and conniving they were.

This is the dividing hatred, and it is the same spirit Peter describes: evil speakers, not afraid to speak evil of dignities, heirs of that mist of darkness. The rulers of the south hated their northern brothers so much that the name of the north was their insult, and the same hatred of brothers is still found today.

precepts.text: Their minds were blinded; the same vail remaineth in the reading of the old testament, done away in Christ; when it shall turn to the Lord, the vail shall be taken away.
precepts.point: Leaders of other camps do not show up at IUIC schools unannounced and then complain on video about not being let in. There are channels; call first. The camps do not fellowship because of doctrine, and one GMS member sat in a school for months living a double life.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
“And not as Moses, which put a vail over his face, that the children of Israel could not stedfastly look to the end of that which is abolished”. Moses spent time with the Lord, and the Lord's glory was upon him so that he was blinding; he had to wear a vail. The shine on Moses represented the new covenant: the glory of Christ was on Moses, and the people could not look at Moses just as they could not see Christ in the Old Testament.

“But their minds were blinded”. Not their eyes; their minds. How is your mind blinded? You read the Bible and say, I don't see it, when it is right there. Nations can't be saved: I don't see it. Israelite: I don't see it. Then, “for until this day remaineth the same vail untaken away in the reading of the old testament; which vail is done away in Christ.” When it comes to reading the Old Testament, they are still blinded as they were with Moses, blinded to Christ and to the northern kingdom being brought back in.

“But even unto this day, when Moses is read, the vail is upon their heart”: they don't understand the prophets. “Nevertheless when it shall turn to the Lord, the vail shall be taken away”: when they repent, they will see Christ. “Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty”, liberty from keeping animal sacrifice.

That is the mist of darkness Peter speaks of, and the only way out of it is turning to the Lord. Keep God's commandments and laws; it works for us.

precepts.text: God spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down and delivered them into chains of darkness.
precepts.point: The angels which kept not their first estate are reserved in everlasting chains under darkness. The sons of God who took the daughters of men were Israelites who fell into fornication.

note.label: All Skinfolk Ain't Kinfolk: Children of Darkness

precepts.why:
“For if God spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment”. The angels that sinned are the sons of God in Genesis. Cast down means cast down from their powerful estate. Delivered into chains of darkness, they came right back as the Pharisees, scribes and Sadducees, who were in darkness.

Luke 16 shows them: “And the Pharisees also, who were covetous, heard all these things: and they derided him. And he said unto them, Ye are they which justify yourselves before men; but God knoweth your hearts: for that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.” Today it is going on podcasts and arguing for fame and attention. Christ then spoke of putting away a wife, because the Pharisees were adulterers and fornicators, and the rich man of his parable was the Pharisees, while Lazarus was the disciples, the people under their rule.

2 Peter 2:10: “But chiefly them that walk after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness, and despise government. Presumptuous are they, selfwilled, they are not afraid to speak evil of dignities.” Jude 8 says the same: “these filthy dreamers defile the flesh, despise dominion, and speak evil of dignities.” It says they are not afraid, which means you are supposed to be afraid. There is a consequence. When you say Paul was a false prophet, call John's camp fake, or disrespect Christ, Moses or the twelve, darkness falls upon you. Then comes nation salvation, and people saying they will start wearing Israeli fringes and yarmulkes and speaking Yiddish.

Christ's parable ends the same way: “Bind him hand and foot, and take him away, and cast him into outer darkness”. He was reserved for darkness from the very beginning; some are predestined for light and some for darkness. “For many are called, but few are chosen.” There are many Israelites, but not all Israel is of Israel.

precepts.text: Noah was the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness.
precepts.point: As Noah prepared the ark to the saving of his house, we must prepare our households for when Christ comes back; that takes the same faith. In the days of Noah they were eating, drinking, and marrying until Noah entered the ark and there was no more chance to repent; so shall the coming of the Son of man be. We have to put on the spirit of Noah.

note.label: Genesis 6: The Sons of God and the Preparing of the Ark

precepts.why:
The Most High “spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly”. Noah was the eighth person, the eight souls of 1 Peter 3:20, and he was a preacher of righteousness.

So while he did all that God commanded him and built the ark, he was also preaching, telling his people to repent, while the longsuffering of the Most High waited for them. They did not, and the flood came upon the world of the ungodly.

precepts.text: Noah was the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness.
precepts.point: Ham saw the nakedness of his father and did not cover him; Shem and Japheth went backward and covered their father without looking. The commandments concerning nakedness were being applied; Leviticus 18 opens those laws.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
Noah drank of the wine and was drunken, but understand Noah’s heart. He was “a preacher of righteousness”, the eighth person saved when the Most High “spared not the old world” and brought “in the flood upon the world of the ungodly”.

He preached repentance for around a hundred years, and everyone he knew outside his house drowned. That is the heavy heart behind the wine. Noah drank too much, but he remained righteous in the eyes of the Most High.

precepts.text: Just Lot was a righteous man, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked.
precepts.point: Lot was a just man. To be just means to do that which is lawful and right, a commandment keeper; righteous Lot was vexed from day to day with the unlawful deeds of the wicked.

note.label: Genesis 11: Babel and the Separation of the Nations

precepts.why:
Peter calls him “just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked: (For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;)”. Lot, the son of Haran who came out of Ur of the Chaldees with Abram, was a just man, one who did that which is lawful and right, and righteous Lot was vexed from day to day with the unlawful deeds of the wicked.

“The Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations, and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished.” He delivered just Lot, and he reserves the unjust for judgment.

precepts.text: The cities were made an example unto those that after should live ungodly, and just Lot was delivered.
precepts.point: Just Lot was delivered, a righteous man vexed from day to day with the filthy conversation and unlawful deeds of the wicked. A righteous man cannot be at home with that conduct.

note.label: Genesis 19: The Destruction of Sodom

precepts.why:
The Lord, “turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned them with an overthrow, making them an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly.” The brimstone and fire that overthrew those cities, all the plain, all the inhabitants and that which grew upon the ground, is an ensample for the ungodly who come after.

“And delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked: (For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;)” Lot had found grace in His sight, and the Lord would not do any thing till he was come to Zoar.

A righteous man cannot be at home with that conduct. Lot lived among them and it vexed his righteous soul from day to day, and just Lot was delivered.

precepts.text: They that walk after the flesh despise government; presumptuous are they, selfwilled, not afraid to speak evil of dignities.
precepts.point: Presumptuously means impulsive and willful: no boundaries, doing things without seeking counsel, led by your own mind, your own opinion, your own emotions instead of leaning on the leadership the Most High set in place. Peter marks that spirit: they walk after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness, despise government, presumptuous are they, selfwilled, not afraid to speak evil of dignities. Despising government, gossiping and murmuring against leadership, and refusing to gather with the body is that same dangerous spirit; the Lord said gather yourselves together, O nation not desired, and he works through spiritual men as he did through Moses and Aaron.

note.label: Leviticus 4: The Sin Offering for Sins of Ignorance

precepts.why:
Peter marks the presumptuous spirit: “them that walk after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness, and despise government. Presumptuous are they, selfwilled, they are not afraid to speak evil of dignities.”

Despising government, gossiping and murmuring against leadership, and refusing to gather with the body is that same dangerous spirit Numbers 15 says shall be cut off. The Lord said gather yourselves together, O nation not desired, and He works through spiritual men as He did through Moses and Aaron. The selfwilled man, led by his own mind and not afraid to speak evil of dignities, is not sinning through ignorance.

precepts.text: They that despise government, presumptuous and selfwilled, are not afraid to speak evil of dignities, the same spirit that speaks against the men the Most High sets up.
precepts.point: He declared the difference: to a prophet He makes Himself known in a vision and speaks in a dream, but with His servant Moses, faithful in all His house, He speaks mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches. Wherefore then were ye not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?

note.label: Numbers 12: Speaking Against the Man of God

precepts.why:
The Lord Himself declared the difference between Moses and a prophet: to a prophet He makes Himself known in a vision and speaks in a dream, but with His servant Moses, “who is faithful in all mine house”, He speaks “mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches.” Then He asked, “wherefore then were ye not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?”

Peter names that spirit: “them that walk after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness, and despise government. Presumptuous are they, selfwilled, they are not afraid to speak evil of dignities.” Miriam and Aaron were not afraid to speak against the man the Most High set up; that is despising government, presumptuous and selfwilled.

It is the same spirit today that speaks against the men the Most High sets up, and Moses was very meek, above all the men upon the face of the earth, when they did it.

note.label: Job 21: Why the Wicked Prosper

Job knows their thoughts and the devices they wrongfully imagine against him when they ask where the house of the prince is and where the dwelling places of the wicked are. Ask them that go by the way. The Most High knows how to deliver the godly out of temptation and to reserve the unjust to the day of judgment to be punished; the wicked's prosperity is only a reservation until the day of wrath.

note.label: Psalm 4: The Lord Hath Set Apart Him That Is Godly for Himself

precepts.point: As a dog returns to his vomit, so a fool returns to his folly. Second Peter calls this a true proverb, showing the apostles quoted Solomon: those who escape the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of Christ and then are again entangled are worse off than at the beginning.

note.label: Proverbs 26: Honor Is Not Fitting for a Fool

precepts.why:
“As a dog returneth to his vomit, so a fool returneth to his folly.” Peter quotes this and calls it a true proverb, which shows the apostles quoted Solomon.

“For if after they have escaped the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, they are again entangled therein, and overcome, the latter end is worse with them than the beginning.” Those who escape the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of Christ and then are again entangled are worse off than at the beginning. “For it had been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than, after they have known it, to turn from the holy commandment delivered unto them.”

Then Peter brings Solomon: “But it is happened unto them according to the true proverb, The dog is turned to his own vomit again; and the sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire.” The fool going back to his folly is the man who knew the way of righteousness and turned from the holy commandment: the dog back at his vomit and the washed sow back in the mire.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 9 Explained Pt. 2

precepts.why:
Woe to them that sin and keep not my commandments; this touches our people just for a moment. “These are wells without water,” Peter gives an analogy about Israelites. You go to a well to get water because you are thirsty, but there is no water in the well. So you have brothers and sisters who appear like they have knowledge, water, understanding, but when you examine them they are wells without water; you see a lot of them on YouTube today. “clouds that are carried with a tempest; to whom the mist of darkness is reserved for ever.” Meaning what? There are certain spirits that are reserved for evil. They come into this truth as brothers, as sisters, but in the end they were reserved for evil. That is what that darkness is.

“For when they speak great swelling words of vanity,” Great swelling words of BS, of lies; it is talking about Israelites now. “they allure through the lusts of the flesh, through much wantonness, those that were clean escaped from them who live in error.” Like Deacon Malachi brought out today: a brother who has been here for some time sees a dumb video that went up in December of last year, and he goes, I've been tricked, I've been fooled, I'm leaving. Evil. Those spirits, and there ain't too many of them, reach out to brothers and sisters that do not apply Romans 16:17, mark them which cause divisions and avoid them. Some of you men and women say, I don't have to obey that, you can't tell me who to talk to. Okay, and this is what happens: they allure you, draw you into their BS, their lies, their evil, through much wantonness, sexual evil, spiritually speaking. Those that were clean escaped from them: that is those of you that remained behind, but you kept entertaining it, listening to them. They were my friends, I'm not cutting them off, I'm not obeying Romans 16:17; I know Christ said if your right hand offend you, cut it off, but I'm not obeying Christ either.

“While they promise them liberty,” They promise you liberty: come with us, you don't have to do what they say, they're not the men of the Lord, come to my house and sit with me and we'll start all over again. Here it is almost a year later: they have not taught one thing on the street, they have not traveled anywhere, they have done absolutely nothing. A brother that was with us left and said, you don't have to go on the street and teach any more. What scripture was that? He didn't have one. Those spirits fool some of you men and women. And this incident here: it is not so much the brother, it is that he is weak; his wife stayed in contact with the wives of the idiots that left, they got in her head, and because he is weak she got in his head. That damn pillow talk: right after you have sex you want to have a conversation. Don't talk to me, I'm tired, go to sleep. But not this brother: let's cuddle, you need to be more affectionate, and she is in his ear, they're wicked, they're evil, we need to go do nothing in the world with the rest of those men and women who love the Lord. He started off good, doing work in Haiti and all that; now look at him doing nothing with his damn buzzard wife. Wicked as hell, but shame on you. The fools that leave this truth promise you liberty: those commandments are a burden, keeping the Sabbath is a burden, you only have to observe the Sabbath from sunup to sundown. Yeah, that's easier, I can go shopping Friday night, I can go to the club Friday night. “they themselves are the servants of corruption:” Those men and women that left this truth are servants of corruption, servants of sin. “for of whom a man is overcome, of the same is he brought in bondage.” Into bondage of sin. Peter was warning us, because it happened back then during the time of the apostles, and it is happening all over again.

“For if after they have escaped the pollutions of the world” You came into this truth, you struggled, you fought to escape the sins of the world. “through the knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ,” How do you escape the sins of this world? Through the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ: he gives us the laws, the commandments; he teaches us where sin begins, in our minds and our thoughts, and we have to start to curb our thinking. “they are again entangled therein,” Because you were listening to them fools that left this truth, you are again entangled, “and overcome, the latter end is worse with them than the beginning.” It is worse with you now than when you first came in. When you first came in you only struggled with porn or weed; now you left the truth and it is all kinds of evil, everything you can think of. “For it had been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than, after they have known it, to turn from the holy commandment delivered unto them.” All those men and women that heard this truth, came in, learned, applied, prayed, saw the benefits of the truth, lives changed, marriages held together through counsel, through the scriptures; now they go, I just hate you, I'm leaving, they're all hate groups. It had been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness.

“But it is happened unto them according to the true proverb, The dog is turned to his own vomit again; and the sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire.” The sow is the pig, and the mire is mud: you washed the pig and it went right back to the mud you washed off it; the dog vomited, then went back and licked it up again. That is every man and woman that left this truth. I don't care if they are on Facebook with fringes on: they are wicked as hell, all of them, every last one of them. Why? Because the evil they said happened in Austin, they put it on everybody: you're all wicked, all the leadership, you all did it. But we are all the way in another part of the country; we don't know what the hell is going on over there. That shows improper judgment. Every last one of them.
